themes.label: Profanity / taboo insults / dehumanizing labels
themes.interpretation: Posts in this theme rely on explicit profanity and derogatory/insulting language to attack people or groups; this is often moderation-relevant because it escalates hostility and can target protected classes or political opponents with abuse.

themes.label: Calls for action / imperatives (prosecute, fight, stop, go after, etc.)
defining_features: imperative or must/stop phrasing (expressed via existing feature values)
themes.interpretation: This theme covers prescriptive, command-like communication urging concrete behavioral or political steps (e.g., “MUST prosecute”, “Stop”, “Go after”). Moderation may focus on whether these are incitement/retaliation-adjacent versus legitimate advocacy.

themes.label: Outgroup vs ingroup framing (us-vs-them / “your side” contrasts)
themes.interpretation: Many posts structure disagreement through in-group/out-group contrasts, blame targeting, or mirror retargeting. This pattern can correlate with escalatory rhetoric and selective moral condemnation.

themes.label: Emphatic punctuation and ALL CAPS for urgency
themes.interpretation: This theme signals high emotional intensity and urgency via capitalization and heavy punctuation. It’s not necessarily abusive by itself, but it frequently accompanies confrontational or extreme claims.

themes.label: Conditional / causal claims about political outcomes and consequences
themes.interpretation: Posts often use ‘if/then’ or cause-and-effect language to argue that policies or election results will lead to major harm. Moderation may examine whether these claims are speculative, fear-mongering, or connected to calls for harmful action.

themes.label: Conspiratorial framing / hoaxes / hidden motives
defining_features: factual_assertion_vs_speculation (when it’s presented as definitive but is conspiracy-like)
conspiratorial framing (coordinated deception, paid supporters, strategic manipulation)
themes.interpretation: This theme attributes events to coordinated deception or covert actors (e.g., “Russian hoax”, “being paid”, naming elites as causes). Such framing is often moderation-relevant due to misinformation risk and can inflame hostility.

themes.label: Policy/legal-domain references (Second Amendment, guns, abortion, immigration, etc.)
themes.interpretation: A large portion of posts are grounded in explicit policy domains (guns/Second Amendment, abortion laws, immigration/citizenship). By itself this is content-appropriate, but it becomes more risky when combined with conspiracies, dehumanizing attacks, or direct violent/retaliatory instructions.

themes.label: Legal/court/case and named proper nouns density
example_message_ids: reddit_1keojcj_mqlr5e2 (Trump Israel etc; but legal case: use twitter_2061570902219760095)
themes.interpretation: Posts that heavily cite named individuals, jurisdictions, or legal/court entities tend to be more ‘argument/documentation’ style. Moderation relevance is higher when these details are paired with abusive or conspiratorial rhetoric.

themes.label: Ridicule / mockery via rhetorical questions, sarcasm, and contemptuous evaluation
themes.interpretation: This theme captures sarcastic or rhetorical challenge styles that delegitimize opponents (including via contempt). It often overlaps with insults/profanity but can also occur without explicit taboo language.

cross_cutting_themes: Profanity / taboo insults / dehumanizing labels overlaps with outgroup framing and ridicule/mockery
Emphatic punctuation / ALL CAPS commonly co-occurs with causal or conditional consequence claims
Calls for action frequently co-occur with policy/legal-domain discussions and moralized urgency
Conspiratorial framing overlaps with causal/conditional consequences and outgroup blame targeting
Named proper nouns density often appears alongside policy/legal-domain references and jurisdiction/court citations
